title: BlueKite Retail — staging & ramp handoff
summary: Kickoff to align staging cutover and pilot ramp for product search embeddings and chat support. Discussed VPC peering timing, SSO, KMS, sample throughput targets, fallbacks, and a small benchmark plan. Agreed next actions: SE to run a targeted perf test, CSM to provide onboarding playbook, customer to open infra tickets for VPC peering and KMS access.
action_items: Marcus D'Souza: run 10k token / 1k qps simulated throughput test in dedicated staging, share results by 2025-08-26
Priya Nair: send onboarding runbook + runbook checklist and sample prompts by 2025-08-23
BlueKite - David Ruiz: open infra ticket for VPC peering + provide subnet details by 2025-08-22
Maya Patel: confirm KMS policy and list of required audit logs by 2025-08-25
next_steps: CSM to schedule weekly 30-min standup for pilot cadence starting 2025-08-27
Exchange staging access creds and a small sample dataset for eval by 2025-08-23
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-08-21 11:00am PT | Duration: ~42m | Recording: yes | Location: Zoom
Attendees: Lena, Priya, Marcus (Redwood) — Oliver, Sara, David, Maya, Ethan (BlueKite)

[00:00] Lena Ortiz: hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick icebreaker, i'm lena from redwood inference — i'll run the cadence stuff. how's every— uh — good morning to east coast folks.
[00:12] Oliver Chen: good morning, lena, thanks. excited to get this moving. we want the staging cutover to be low friction, we have late august as a soft target.
[00:21] Priya Nair: hi! priya here, i'll own the onboarding and success runway, so i'll be your main point for checklists, runbooks etc.
[00:27] Sara Kim: sara — operations. our main concerns: network setup, SSO, KMS for data encryption and audit logs.
[00:35] Marcus D'Souza: marcus — SE. i'll run the perf and help with model/quant recommendations and batching profiles.
[00:40] Ethan Park: hey all, ethan — ML engineer; we'll be testing embeddings and chat responses, and run some evaluation on latency.
[00:46] Lena Ortiz: cool. agenda — align staging timeline, confirm infra next steps, perf targets, and handoff of runbook. anything to add?
[00:53] Oliver Chen: maybe fallback policies — if we hit capacity in hosted we want clear fallback to a cheaper variant or cached responses.
[01:00] Marcus D'Souza: yeah we recommend a tiered routing policy: hosted default, dedicated fallback, and a cold-cache static response for noncritical flows. we'll propose specifics after the perf run.
[01:12] David Ruiz: quick question — for VPC peering, do you support AWS Direct Connect style peering or is it just VPC peering? our infra team prefers private connectivity.
[01:22] Priya Nair: currently for private we support VPC peering and transit gateway setups; direct connect would be partner/network-level — we can map it in the runbook.
[01:30] Maya Patel: about KMS: we need to ensure customer-managed keys for both transit and at-rest. also SOC 2 audit log granularity — can we get token-level event logs?
[01:41] Marcus D'Souza: we support customer-managed KMS for private deployments; logs are emitted to your logging stack (S3/ELK) — token-level is sensitive but we have event-level traces and can discuss redaction. sometimes the auto-transcript mislabels things; we'll produce an audit sample.
[01:58] Lena Ortiz: good — noted. target pilot SLOs — what are you expecting for latency/throughput?
[02:04] Oliver Chen: ballpark: 100ms median for short chat turns, 95th under 400ms, and embeddings at 200ms p95. throughput initially 200 qps, ramp to 1k during peak.
[02:16] Marcus D'Souza: that's fair. i'll run 200 qps and a 1k qps sim with sequences that match your histograms. quick note: depending on sequence length and batching this will vary — our runtime selects kernels by seq length distribution.
[02:29] Ethan Park: our average prompt is about 120 tokens, with a 350-token response cap in some flows.
[02:34] Marcus D'Souza: perfect, that'll shape batching strategy. we'll share a suggested batching config (e.g., max batch size, timeout) in the perf report.
[02:42] Sara Kim: what's the expected effort from our side for instrumentation? we want tracing tied to our SRE stack.
[02:48] Priya Nair: we'll provide tracing hooks and an example for Datadog and NewRelic. for private customers we also expose per-route telemetry and token level cost maps; we'll send the template.
[02:59] David Ruiz: is RBAC and SAML available out of box? how granular?
[03:05] Marcus D'Souza: yes SAML SSO + SCIM for provisioning; RBAC supports roles (admin, dev, viewer) and per-route model access controls.
[03:14] Maya Patel: any gotchas with data residency? we have EU workloads that must stay in eu-west-1.
[03:20] Lena Ortiz: you can pin regions, and for private we support local on-prem options. we'll note region pinning in the runbook.
[03:28] Oliver Chen: ok great. can we talk about fallback behavior again — if we fall back to quantized model, how much quality delta should we expect?
[03:36] Marcus D'Souza: typical tradeoff: 5-8% dip in some semantic retrieval tasks; generative chat often shows small regressions, but we can do A/B tests. we also support automatic gradual rollout.
[03:49] Ethan Park: are you doing prefix KV caching? we have a lot of repeated system prompts.
[03:54] Marcus D'Souza: yes, prefix/KV cache is supported — that'll dramatically reduce token cost for repeated contexts. we'll recommend cache TTLs.
[04:03] Lena Ortiz: let's surface the concrete timeline. priya?
[04:06] Priya Nair: we propose: this week (aug 21) — infra tickets and creds exchanged; week of aug 24 — SE perf tests and initial results; aug 27 — first pilot standup; sept 2 — cutover to staging and begin production-run ramp. open to adjusting.
[04:23] Oliver Chen: sept 2 is tight but doable. we need the perf data before we commit.
[04:28] Marcus D'Souza: i'll push results by aug 26 to give you 3 days to review.
[04:32] David Ruiz: i'll open the VPC peering ticket today and add subnets and contact info.
[04:36] Maya Patel: i'll send over the KMS policy requirements. also need the SOC 2 cert and ISO artifacts.
[04:44] Lena Ortiz: yes, we'll share the security pack and SOC 2 letter — priya will attach.
[04:49] Sara Kim: any immediate blockers we've missed?
[04:52] Ethan Park: curious about pricing delta for dedicated vs hosted for the pilot — ballpark numbers?
[04:57] Priya Nair: i'll send an indicative price sheet for pilot economics — not final procurement numbers but enough to plan capacity.
[05:05] Oliver Chen: for procurement we'll engage later; for now confirm that logs and audit trail will be preserved for 90 days.
[05:12] Marcus D'Souza: yes, default retention 90 days for observability; longer retention is an add-on.
[05:19] Lena Ortiz: great. last part: runbook handoff — priya will create a shared google doc with onboarding checklist, access steps, network diagram, and playbook runbook.
[05:29] Priya Nair: i'll populate and invite all of you by tomorrow.
[05:33] Lena Ortiz: OK let's recap. Marcus will run perf and share by 2025-08-26; Priya sends runbook and security pack by 2025-08-23; BlueKite to open infra tickets and share KMS details by 2025-08-22/25; schedule weekly 30min standup starting 2025-08-27. any objections?
[05:51] Oliver Chen: sounds good. one more micro note: can you include a sample of audit log fields so our compliance team can pre-approve?
[05:58] Marcus D'Souza: yes, i'll include a redacted sample.
[06:02] Lena Ortiz: awesome. thanks everyone — we'll follow up in email with links and action items. meeting adjourned.

Optional notes: shared artifacts referenced during call: onboarding runbook (link to be shared), performance benchmark spreadsheet (to be shared), security pack (SOC2 + ISO)

End of transcript.
